stories.title: Vacant 304-Unit Pembroke Pines Condo Community Trades for $20.5M
stories.excerpt: The 304-unit Heron Pond condominium community in Pembroke Pines was acquired by Integra for $20.5 million. All units located on the property have been vacated due to safety concerns, resulting in the Receivership and the termination of the Condominium Association, thereby allowing the Receiver to market and sell as a single fee simple sale. Offered on an “as-is” basis, the site sits in an infill location in Pembroke Pines. The in-place zoning allows for up to 321 units by right, and the unit count could more than double through upzoning or a land use plan map amendment. Avison Young and Fisher Auction arranged the sale of the condominium complex. Avison Young John K. Crotty, David Duckworth, Michael T. Fay and Brian C. de la Fé, along with Fisher Auction Company CEO Lamar Fisher and Executive Vice President Paul Fisher, led the marketing and auction process. The post Vacant 304-Unit Pembroke Pines Condo Community Trades for $20.5M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Integra acquires 304-unit vacant Pembroke Pines condo for $20.5M as fee-simple receivership sale.
Zoning allows 321 units by-right; potential upzoning could double unit count on infill site.
Distressed asset purchased as-is; value-add redevelopment play in South Florida market.
stories.summary: Integra acquired the 304-unit Heron Pond condominium in Pembroke Pines, Florida for $20.5 million in a receivership sale. All units were vacated due to safety concerns, enabling sale as a single fee-simple asset. The in-fill site is currently zoned for 321 units by-right, with potential to more than double through upzoning or land use amendment. The transaction represents a distressed acquisition likely structured for repositioning and conversion.
stories.impact: This signals a **redevelopment opportunity in Broward County (Pembroke Pines)** where a large vacant multifamily footprint can be repositioned or densified. The as-is sale price ($67.4K/unit) and unit-count upside suggest the buyer expects significant value creation through capital investment and/or regulatory approval—a clear play on market demand recovery and zoning upside in South Florida's multifamily sector.

stories.title: Good Office Design Is Good Business
stories.excerpt: In the summer of 2023, Greatland Realty Partners and Barings acquired an approximately 515,000-square-foot office campus at 275 Grove Street in Newton, Mass., for $117.5 million. The property had last traded just three years earlier for $235 million. It was almost 40 percent vacant for the first time in its 25-year history. The market was skeptical. Less than two years later, Global Partners LP — a Fortune 500 company that had occupied its previous headquarters for 34 years — acquired an equity interest in the building and signed a long-term, 125,000-square-foot lease. Common area utilization had been transformed, and the asset was stabilized. What happened in between was not a cosmetic refresh and not a gut renovation. It was a disciplined, strategy-driven reinvestment in the building’s shared amenities and common spaces that demonstrates a simple principle: Design, executed with business objectives in mind, is one of the most effective tools for protecting and enhancing asset value. Elizabeth Lowrey. Photo: Trevor Reid For more than two decades, 275 Grove Street was the premier suburban office complex in the Newton market. Developed in 2000 from a former warehouse, it was the building companies loved and rarely left. Then, in 2020, the previous owner acquired the property with plans to convert it to laboratory space. When the lab market softened in 2022, the owner pivoted to a motivated sale. Greatland and Barings saw what others missed: a building with exceptional bones, strong location and unrealized potential in a market that had written off the asset. The data supports the bet. From 2020 to 2024, prime buildings nationally registered 48 million square feet of positive net absorption while the rest of the office market lost 170 million square feet of occupancy. bullets: Office campus trades at major loss: $117.5M purchase (2023) vs. $235M sale (2020).
Fortune 500 tenant (Global Partners LP) signs 125K SF lease after common-area redesign.
Strategic amenity investment stabilized 40%-vacant property; design-driven turnaround, not gut renovation.
stories.summary: Greatland Realty Partners and Barings acquired a 515,000-square-foot office campus at 275 Grove Street in Newton, Massachusetts for $117.5 million in summer 2023, down from a $235 million sale price just three years prior. The property had reached 40% vacancy for the first time in its 25-year history. Less than two years post-acquisition, Global Partners LP—a Fortune 500 company—acquired an equity stake and signed a long-term 125,000-square-foot lease. The turnaround was driven by disciplined reinvestment in shared amenities and common spaces, not a full renovation.
stories.impact: **Not directly applicable to multifamily development**, but the narrative underscores how **office distress and tenant flight are reshaping suburban markets like Boston's Route 128 corridor**. For multifamily: this loss of office stability may signal weaker local employment and demographic tailwinds for nearby residential in the Newton submarket, requiring deeper diligence on job-creation anchors before underwriting new apartment communities nearby.

stories.title: JV Sells 8-Building Jax Warehouse Portfolio for $35M
stories.excerpt: A joint venture of East Capital Partners and Tranview Capital offloaded an eight-building multitenant industrial portfolio for $35 million. The 230,000-square-foot Airport Jax Small Bay Portfolio was 92% leased at the time. It’s being rebranded at InSpace at Jax. A CBRE team made up of Kyle Fisher and Kyle Murphy represented the sellers. NorthBridge Partners was the buyer. Located at 14475 Duval Place West in Jacksonville’s Northside industrial submarket, the portfolio has a diverse mix of 45 tenants across a range of industries. The property is less than one mile from Interstate 95 and approximately 2.5 miles from Jacksonville International Airport. The transaction underscores continued investor interest in Jacksonville’s industrial market, particularly in the Northside submarket. CBRE Research reported approximately 1.3 million square feet of leasing activity in Northside during the second quarter, while the overall Jacksonville market posted nearly 583,000 square feet of positive net absorption and declining vacancy. The post JV Sells 8-Building Jax Warehouse Portfolio for $35M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: East Capital Partners and Tranview Capital sell 8-building, 230K SF industrial portfolio for $35M.
Northside Jacksonville Jax Airport submarket: 92% leased, 45-tenant mix, repositioned as InSpace.
Q2 Northside showed 1.3M SF leasing activity; overall Jax market had positive net absorption, declining vacancy.
stories.summary: A joint venture of East Capital Partners and Tranview Capital sold the eight-building, 230,000-square-foot Airport Jax Small Bay Portfolio (rebranded as InSpace at Jax) for $35 million to NorthBridge Partners. The portfolio was 92% leased with 45 tenants at sale. Located at 14475 Duval Place West in Jacksonville's Northside submarket, the asset benefits from proximity to I-95 and Jacksonville International Airport. CBRE data shows the Northside submarket recorded 1.3 million square feet of Q2 leasing activity, with the broader Jacksonville market posting positive net absorption and declining vacancy.
stories.impact: **Jacksonville's industrial market—specifically the Northside submarket—is demonstrating strong leasing velocity and investor appetite, signaling sustained demand for logistics and light-manufacturing tenants.** For multifamily: this industrial strength suggests job and population stability in Jacksonville's north corridor, supporting rental demand in nearby residential communities. Developers should consider Class B/C multifamily acquisition or ground-up development in Northside or adjacent submarkets that capture workers employed at these industrial parks.

stories.title: Gowanus Golf Club Secures 6K SF to Open Private Club in Brooklyn’s Dumbo
stories.excerpt: A new golf club is being teed up for Brooklyn’s Dumbo neighborhood. Gowanus Golf Club, a Brooklyn-based private indoor golf club chain, has leased approximately 6,000 square feet along the Dumbo waterfront at 215 Water Street, Commercial Observer has learned. The five-story mixed-use building between Bridge and Jay streets is owned by Pearl Realty Management, according to broker Corey Cohen, principal of the Roebling team at Compass. The length of the lease was not disclosed, but the asking rent was $100 per square foot. “Dumbo’s continued residential growth, particularly at the luxury end of the market, has created a natural audience for premium, membership-driven concepts,” Cohen, who represented both the landlord and the tenant, said in a statement. “Gowanus Golf Club needed both the physical scale to deliver its full experience and a neighborhood with the density and year-round activity to support it. At 215 Water Street, those requirements came together.” The new golf club, set to open in mid-September, will feature simulator bays, a members lounge, a putting area and fitness equipment, as well as a repair shop and wellness rooms. The club will also offer league and tournament events as well as golf lessons. The deal represents a new location for Gowanus Golf Club, which has two existing Brooklyn clubs at 124 Ninth Street in Gowanus and 646 Dean Street in Prospect Heights, according to its website. “Gowanus Golf Club is more than an indoor golf facility,” Jordan Colina, founder of Gowanus Golf Club, said in a statement. “Our goal is to create a private membership club where golfers can improve their game, meet other players and enjoy premium amenities in a welcoming setting. Dumbo’s vibrant community made it an easy choice for the next addition to our network of locations, and we’re excited to welcome members soon.” Other tenants at 215 Water Street include toy manufacturer Little Poland Gallery and appliance store VMN & Company. Isabelle Durso can be reach
bullets: Gowanus Golf Club leases 6K SF at 215 Water Street, Dumbo (Brooklyn) at $100/SF.
Luxury residential growth in Dumbo creating demand for premium membership-driven amenity uses.
Mixed-use building owned by Pearl Realty Management; club opens mid-September.
stories.summary: Gowanus Golf Club, a Brooklyn-based private indoor golf club chain, leased approximately 6,000 square feet at 215 Water Street in Brooklyn's Dumbo neighborhood for $100 per square foot. The five-story mixed-use building between Bridge and Jay streets is owned by Pearl Realty Management. The lease signals demand for premium, membership-driven experience venues driven by Dumbo's continued luxury residential growth and year-round population density. The club is set to open in mid-September.
stories.impact: **Dumbo's residential absorption and rent growth are now strong enough to anchor premium lifestyle amenities, a secondary indicator of market maturity.** For multifamily developers: Dumbo's continued luxury-end residential growth justifies higher rents and capital spend on in-building amenities and experiential programming. This leasing also confirms limited Class-A retail/amenity space availability in the neighborhood, suggesting pricing power for residential developers offering integrated lifestyle offerings.

stories.title: Multifamily Comprises 80% of CRE CLO Collateral in Recent Deals
stories.excerpt: A handful of the latest commercial real estate collateralized loan obligation (CLO) deals lean hard into multifamily collateral and full-term interest-only structures. CRED iQ analyzed loan-level collateral across a handful of the latest CRE CLO deals totaling $4.68 billion and 160 loans of collateral with the profile pointing to lenders concentrating risk in the sectors and structures they trust most in a higher-rate environment. Apartment collateral makes up 79.8 percent of aggregate balance in the sample, followed by hospitality at 8.1 percent and industrial at 5.2 percent. Office, retail and health care each account for roughly 1 percent or less. The concentration confirms that CRE CLO issuers remain committed to transitional multifamily lending even as other property types stay largely on the sidelines. Interest-only (IO) terms are nearly universal. Full-term IO loans represent 95 percent of collateral balance, with the small remainder carrying partial IO or amortization. The structure preserves borrower cash flow as business plans are executed, but it also means principal paydown is minimal until maturity, keeping refinancing pressure front and center. The sampled pools carry a weighted-average spread of 303 basis points over the Secured Oversight Financing Rate and a weighted-average coupon near 6.68 percent. These deals point to a familiar core: multifamily assets, floating-rate coupons, and IO structures that maximize early cash flow. Future funding commitments total $244 million across these deals, signaling continued appetite to finance value-add and lease-up business plans. Geographic exposure skews toward New York, Florida and Texas, which together account for more than 43 percent of balance. For investors, the takeaway is concentration. bullets: Multifamily comprises 79.8% of $4.68B in recent CRE CLO collateral across 160 loans.
95% of collateral carries full-term interest-only structure; principal paydown deferred until maturity.
Office, retail, healthcare each under 1%; hospitality 8.1%, industrial 5.2% of CLO pools.
stories.summary: A CRED iQ analysis of $4.68 billion in recent CRE CLO deals totaling 160 loans found apartment collateral comprises 79.8% of aggregate balance. Hospitality accounts for 8.1%, industrial 5.2%, while office, retail, and healthcare each represent roughly 1% or less. Nearly all loans (95% of collateral balance) carry full-term interest-only structures, deferring principal paydown until maturity and preserving borrower cash flow during business-plan execution. The concentration reflects CRE lender confidence in transitional multifamily lending despite higher rates.
stories.impact: **Multifamily lending remains the sole asset class attracting significant capital through CLO structures in a higher-rate environment, signaling confidence in NOI stability and exit potential.** For developers: this dominance of apartment collateral in CLOs means **financing availability and pricing for multifamily acquisitions and construction are more favorable than other property types**, creating a window for capital-efficient development. However, the universal IO structure means refinancing pressure is front-loaded; developers should model exit assumptions conservatively given minimal principal paydown.

stories.title: Technology Platform Genius AI Expands by 14K SF at 838 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Technology platform Genius AI, formerly known as GlossGenius, has undertaken a 13,754-square-foot headquarters expansion at ZG Capital Partners’ 838 Broadway, Commercial Observer has learned. The deal sees Genius AI’s footprint at 838 Broadway grow to 27,373 square feet, occupying the entire second and third floors. The deal also secures 100 percent occupancy for the six-story building, located between East 12th and East 13th streets just south of Union Square. Lease terms were not disclosed, but asking rent at the building was $110 per square foot as recently as November. JLL’s Joseph Sipala, Stefanie Rock, Finley Burger and Hannah Bernstein represented the tenant, while another JLL team of Mitch Konsker, Ben Bass, Thomas Swartz and Greg Wang negotiated on behalf of ZG Capital Partners. Genius AI arrived at the freshly renovated and repositioned 838 Broadway in 2024, taking 13,619 square feet across the second floor. Originally conceived as a spa- and salon-booking startup, the firm has had a repositioning of its own, transforming into an artificial intelligence platform for small businesses. Sipala told Commercial Observer that he began working with the company three years ago, when he helped them relocate from a small SoHo loft to 838 Broadway. “Today they occupy multiple floors, backed by strong momentum and a raise,” Sipala said. “Being part of their journey, and helping to shape their real estate strategy at every stage, continues to be a privilege.” News of Genius AI’s office expansion coincides with the female-founded tech firm’s most recent $44 million fundraising round, which secured it a $1.15 billion unicorn valuation. “Genius AI exists to bring AI to the part of the economy that doesn’t [sit] behind a screen — businesses built on face-to-face service,” Danielle Cohen-Shohet, CEO and co-founder of Genius AI, said in a statement. “So it’s fitting that our next chapter doubles down on an investment in physical space.” The office building
bullets: Genius AI expands 13.7K SF at ZG Capital's 838 Broadway (Manhattan); total footprint grows to 27.4K SF.
Expansion secures 100% occupancy across entire second and third floors of six-story building.

stories.summary: Technology platform Genius AI (formerly GlossGenius) undertook a 13,754-square-foot headquarters expansion at 838 Broadway in Manhattan, growing its footprint to 27,373 square feet and occupying the entire second and third floors. The deal achieved 100% occupancy for the six-story building located between East 12th and East 13th streets just south of Union Square. The property, recently renovated and repositioned by owner ZG Capital Partners, reflected asking rents of $110 per square foot as of November.
stories.impact: **Not directly applicable to multifamily development**, but signals sustained tech-company demand and strong office occupancy in the Union Square submarket despite broader NYC office headwinds. For multifamily: this expansion confirms Union Square South and Flatiron remain desirable for high-growth tech tenants, supporting neighborhood rents and population density. Developers should view this as demand validation for new residential in Lower Manhattan/NoMad, where proximity to Union Square tech clusters drives young professional migration.

stories.title: Rick Gropper of Camber Property Group: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: New York-based Camber Property Group is celebrating a decade in business this year, and Rick Gropper, principal and co-founder of the firm, said it’s the company’s busiest year yet. Founded in 2016 by Gropper and Andrew Moelis, the real estate development and management firm specializes in building and preserving affordable, mixed-use and transitional multifamily housing. Camber’s name was at the forefront of two major housing announcements this summer. One of them was the start of construction for the $167 million redevelopment of Chelsea Beacon, where 131 affordable units, supportive housing, and community spaces will replace the former Bayview Correctional Facility at 550 West 20th Street. Plus, Camber was one of the developers selected for the $62 million modernization of NYCHA’s Unity Towers in Coney Island. The firm is also growing its national portfolio, bringing its experience in turning around distressed assets and building new housing to Pennsylvania, Connecticut, New Jersey and Ohio. Commercial Observer sat down with Gropper in July to discuss the two headline-making projects, what it took for Camber to get there, and the challenges ahead. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Tell us about your background. I interned for a year before they finally hired me. I worked my way up from an assistant project manager to a project manager, and I was able to learn all aspects of the development process. bullets: Camber Property Group celebrates decade of operations; 2024 is company's busiest year.
Chelsea Beacon: $167M redevelopment of former Bayview Correctional Facility; 131 affordable units.
NYCHA Unity Towers (Coney Island): $62M modernization; firm expanding to PA, CT, NJ, OH.
stories.summary: Camber Property Group, a New York-based affordable and mixed-use multifamily developer founded in 2016, reported 2024 as its busiest year a decade in. The firm is leading two major projects: the $167 million redevelopment of Chelsea Beacon (131 affordable units and supportive housing on the site of the former Bayview Correctional Facility at 550 West 20th Street) and a $62 million modernization of NYCHA's Unity Towers in Coney Island. Camber is expanding its national portfolio into Pennsylvania, Connecticut, New Jersey, and Ohio, leveraging expertise in distressed asset repositioning and affordable housing development.
stories.impact: **Camber's national expansion and sustained pipeline of public-sector and preservation deals signal strong capital availability and policy support for affordable multifamily development.** For competitors: the firm's growth into secondary markets (PA, CT, NJ, OH) suggests these geographies are now attracting capital and regulatory incentives for affordable housing. The scale of its NYC projects (Chelsea Beacon, NYCHA partnerships) indicates deep relationships with municipal agencies and mixed-finance structures that create defensible competitive moats—developers seeking to enter affordable multifamily should study Camber's playbook on public-private partnerships.

stories.title: Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater
stories.excerpt: The Trust for Gov­er­nors Island has released a Request for Expres­sions of Inter­est (RFEI) for the revi­tal­iza­tion of two his­toric build­ings on the Island, Build­ing 324 and Build­ing 330. The RFEI invites ideas from prospec­tive part­ners for the revi­tal­iza­tion of these his­toric assets, bring­ing them back into active, year-round use. The Trust seeks respons­es that pro­pose arts and cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, or oth­er pub­lic-fac­ing uses. The two adja­cent build­ings are locat­ed with­in the Gov­er­nors Island His­toric Dis­trict. Orig­i­nal­ly con­struct­ed as a YMCA recre­ation cen­ter and a movie the­ater, respec­tive­ly, the build­ings fea­ture high ceil­ings and open floor plans.  “The for­mer YMCA and Fort Jay The­ater his­tor­i­cal­ly stood as cul­tur­al anchors of Gov­er­nors Island, and we’re thrilled to present a unique oppor­tu­ni­ty to breathe new life into these icon­ic build­ings,” said Clare New­man, pres­i­dent and CEO of the Trust for Gov­er­nors Island. ​“We’re seek­ing vision­ary part­ners with bold ideas for cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, and pub­lic-fac­ing uses that can turn untapped poten­tial into vibrant spaces for every­one to enjoy.” The com­plete RFEI can be viewed here. Submissions are due by Oct. 26. The post Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trust for Governors Island issues RFEI for revitalization of two historic buildings (Buildings 324, 330).
Former YMCA and movie theater to be redeveloped for arts, cultural, or recreational uses.
High ceilings and open floor plans; seeking year-round activation and public-facing uses.
stories.summary: The Trust for Governors Island released a Request for Expressions of Interest (RFEI) for the revitalization of Buildings 324 and 330, two historic structures on the island originally built as a YMCA recreation center and movie theater. The Trust seeks proposals for arts, cultural, recreational, or public-facing uses that will activate these assets year-round. Both buildings are located within the Governors Island Historic District and feature high ceilings and open floor plans.
stories.impact: **Not directly relevant to multifamily development**, but Governors Island's public-realm focus and landmark status make it a destination for lifestyle/hospitality tenants rather than residential. However, if either building is repurposed for hospitality, dining, or cultural uses, it could drive visitation and spending on the island, potentially strengthening the market case for future residential development on Governors Island. Developers should monitor RFEI award timing and use-type to gauge island activation trends.

stories.title: 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced that Deferred, the first and only technology-powered qualified intermediary transforming 1031 exchanges for everyday real estate investors, has joined Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program as a provider of 1031 exchange solutions. The relationship is designed to provide Marcus & Millichap’s clients with streamlined access to qualified intermediary services and technology-enabled 1031 exchange solutions. As interest rates, tax considerations, and market conditions continue to influence investment decisions, many commercial real estate owners seek ways to maximize after-tax proceeds while maintaining purchasing power. Through this relationship, Marcus & Millichap’s clients will gain access to Deferred’s exchange platform, educational resources, and experienced exchange professionals. “1031 exchanges remain one of the most effective tools available to investors seeking to preserve equity and reposition capital,” said Richard Matricaria, chief growth officer of Marcus & Millichap. “Deferred provides a modern, client-focused approach to guiding investors through the exchange process. Their combination of expertise, service and technology makes them a valuable addition to our Preferred Partner Program.” The post 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap partners with Deferred, tech-enabled 1031 exchange qualified intermediary.
1031 exchanges remain primary capital-redeployment tool for CRE investors amid rate and tax pressures.
Streamlined platform designed to preserve equity and maximize after-tax proceeds for exchangers.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap announced that Deferred, a technology-powered qualified intermediary, has joined its Preferred Partner Program to provide streamlined 1031 exchange solutions to clients. The partnership is designed to help CRE owners preserve equity and reposition capital amid rising interest rates and tax considerations. Deferred's platform combines technology, educational resources, and professional guidance to guide investors through 1031 exchange mechanics.
stories.impact: **This partnership signals strong ongoing demand for 1031 exchange tools, indicating that existing CRE owners—including multifamily operators—are actively repositioning capital rather than holding or refinancing in place.** For developers: continued 1031 exchange activity suggests liquidity and deal flow among institutional multifamily sellers, creating both acquisition targets (stabilized assets being exchanged out of) and potential equity partners or JV structures. Monitor Marcus & Millichap transaction volume and 1031-related deal flow as an early indicator of portfolio turnover cycles in major multifamily markets.

stories.title: Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty
stories.excerpt: Greystone has provided a total of $91,851,000 in Fannie Mae loans to refinance and acquire three affordable housing communities located in New York. The financing was originated by senior managing director Eric Rosenstock and EVP Jeff Englund on behalf of Metropolitan Realty Group. The financing includes three affordable multifamily communities that will each undergo moderate rehabilitation as part of the transaction. Built in 1975, Pine Town Houses is a 130-unit garden-style apartment community in Long Beach, NY. Hudson View II and III, in Northern Manhattan’s Hamilton Heights neighborhood, total 129 apartments and 11 commercial spaces. Ariel Property Advisors recently arranged the Hudson View II and III acquisition. Each non-recourse, fixed-rate Fannie Mae loan features a 10-year term with five years of interest-only payments, followed by a 35-year amortization schedule. All three properties are supported by long-term Section 8 Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) contracts and are subject to long-term affordability restrictions.  The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Greystone provides $91.85M in Fannie Mae loans to Metropolitan Realty Group for three NY communities.
Pine Town Houses (Long Beach, NY): 130 units; Hudson View II & III (Hamilton Heights): 140 units.
10-year term with 5-year IO, then 35-year amortization; all properties backed by Section 8 HAP contracts.
stories.summary: Greystone provided a total of $91.85 million in Fannie Mae loans on behalf of Metropolitan Realty Group to refinance and acquire three affordable multifamily communities in New York. Pine Town Houses is a 130-unit garden-style community in Long Beach built in 1975; Hudson View II and III in Northern Manhattan's Hamilton Heights total 129 apartments and 11 commercial spaces. All three loans are non-recourse, fixed-rate, 10-year term with five years of interest-only followed by 35-year amortization. All properties are backed by long-term Section 8 HAP contracts and subject to long-term affordability restrictions.
stories.impact: **Fannie Mae's active financing of legacy affordable multifamily with Section 8 backing indicates strong institutional appetite for stabilized, government-subsidized rental income streams.** For developers: this transaction validates the underwriting model for affordable preservation/refinance deals in NYC submarkets (Long Beach, Hamilton Heights), where mature communities with HAP contracts attract institutional capital at favorable terms. Developers holding or acquiring similar assets should model Fannie Mae DUS programs as primary financing source; the availability of 35-year amortization post-IO tail preserves cash flow during value-add periods.
